Repeat consumption is a legitimate recommendation task ([RepeatNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02646)). Methodological implication: distinguish novelty-only audits, excluding targets previously seen anywhere in complete pre-target history, from repeat-capable audits retaining those targets. Filtering alternatives against complete history while restoring a repeated target creates a third, asymmetric population; label it explicitly. Sample unique alternatives without replacement, excluding the target and padding; freeze prefix IDs and candidate IDs across paired perturbations. These diagnostic pools remain separate from the pinned validation benchmark: sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog metrics ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

For exact-score ties, directly derived target-rank bounds are [1 + number strictly above, 1 + number strictly above + number of tied alternatives]. Report paired rank changes with an explicit sign convention and fixed tie policy; under arbitrary tie-breaking, change bounds are [perturbed lower − original upper, perturbed upper − original lower]. Multiple prefixes per user are dependent: bootstrap whole users, retaining paired observations, and specify prefix-weighted versus user-weighted aggregation. With at most 32 users, intervals are exploratory, conditional on sampled users/candidates and the fitted model; additional prefixes or bootstrap draws do not supply independent users. Few-cluster simulation findings depend on design and do not establish reliable coverage here ([Huang](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5965657/)).

Further diagnostics add evidence beyond an order audit only through distinct, prespecified hypotheses. Prospectively record diagnostic predictions and proposed changes, then compare against an unchanged baseline on the separate fixed macro HR@10 benchmark. Attribute benefit to diagnostic guidance through a matched-budget comparison against unguided search. Repeated validation-driven selection remains adaptive and optimistic; final generalization requires untouched evaluation, and diagnostic bootstrap intervals cannot correct selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).
